findings.title: C6 omits an additional boundary-hollow artifact-load test
findings.detail: The name and docstring claim that an artifact carrying an invalid parameter can be loaded, but lines 307-311 only mutate an in-memory config and construct Model(cfg). The real Model.load path reads and restores the artifact at lizyml/core/_model_persistence.py:345-377. A repository search found no sibling that calls Model.load with not_a_lightgbm_parameter. This NEGATIVE row is HOLLOW under the supplied rule. The boundary-repair population is therefore at least 10 rather than 9, or 13 tests when the three acknowledged weak/contradictory side findings are included. The broader conclusion that most of 231 rows are noun-matching artifacts still follows, but the stated repair population does not.

findings.title: Two OVERCLAIM siblings do not cover the same complete claim
findings.detail: test_metric_default_per_task covers both regression and binary, while its named sibling at tests/test_estimators/test_lgbm_user_metric.py:89-112 trains only binary; the regression branch never reaches a Booster. test_balanced_binary_shifts_predictions claims a prediction shift, but its named sibling at tests/test_training/test_cv_refit_parity.py:186-229 only proves scale_pos_weight reaches training. The separate test_scale_pos_weight_changes_predictions at lines 273-295 supplies that parameter directly and does not exercise balanced=True. Under the requested same-task/parameter/branch rule, both rows are HOLLOW, not OVERCLAIM.

findings.title: The acknowledged side findings also falsify C5's category totals
findings.detail: The objective test accepts TypeError at lines 201-207 even though its enclosing contract requires LizyMLError(CONFIG_INVALID), so an unrelated hash/type failure satisfies the alleged gate. The metrics test asserts only inside if calibrated in result; both a missing branch and an empty calibrated dict pass, despite the claim that empty branches are removed. The codegen test is named no_calibration_fields while its docstring and assertions require those fields to exist as None/5, making the claim genuinely unclear. Thus NEGATIVE 52, UNIT 170, and UNCLEAR 0 cannot all be correct even though C7 correctly reports these weaknesses.

findings.title: The remaining HOLLOW/OVERCLAIM checks and kill mechanism are supported
findings.detail: Both original HOLLOW rows are genuine: test_oof_pred_is_ndarray asserts a value installed by its fixture, and the plot-theme test checks only imported attributes. The other five OVERCLAIM siblings reach the same boundary: fold count, fit override precedence, real FitResult metrics, no-calibration behavior, and binary Platt calibration folds. The kill plugin arms during pytest_configure and patches live module/class attributes; no production from-lightgbm-import-train alias was found. The sampled contextlib.suppress(Exception) row installs a spy that records before delegating to the killed function, so a producer call would fail its empty-call assertion. No table row was found that replaces a killed producer without delegating, catches ProducerRan while still satisfying its assertions, or depends on a pre-armed module/session fixture.

findings.title: C7(a) is confirmed, and the weighted sample otherwise supports UNIT/NEGATIVE
findings.detail: Repository-wide caller search found build_calibration_splitter only at its definition and in tests/documentation. The production calibration path instead reuses fit_result.splits.outer at lizyml/core/model.py:852-865, and tests/test_splitters/test_purged_embargo_merge.py:279-289 exercises that real binary/Platt path. I read 28 UNIT and 14 NEGATIVE rows, weighted toward propagation, prediction, fit, split, metric, and refusal names; apart from the rows reported above, their assertions matched their scoped unit or refusal claims. Targeted pytest execution was attempted but unavailable because pytest was absent from PATH and the fixed runner snapshot prohibited uv cache creation.
